text.p: Analysts at Societe Generale Bank and Trust have upgraded the shares of shoes-to-guns maker Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG to outperform from neutral as they believe the market has over-reacted to the possibility that Bally chief executive Ernst Thomke would resign.

Analyst Hugo Schneider also wrote in a note that the pressure on Oerlikon's share price was heightened by stories in Swiss media that Oerlikon's six-month results at the end of August would be less than sparkling.
However, Schneider wrote that the turnaround of Oerlikon unit Bally was well under way and the possible loss of Thomke would, at worst, slow down the recovery.

In the event that Thomke were to leave Bally, Schneider said the hit to the share price would be limited to 130 Swiss francs, but he still cautioned risk-adverse investors to await the outcome of the board meeting on August 18.
Oerlikon's shares rose 30.9 percent from the beginning of the year until June 26, but since then it has fallen 16.6 percent to 144.00 francs on Friday.
On August 18 Thomke, a renowed turn-around specialist in Switzerland, is due to make an internal presentation at an annual Oerlikon strategy session on his plans to revamp Bally.

Disagreements between Thomke and Oerlikon executives spilled into the public arena in June, when Hortense Anda-Buerhle, the dominant Buehrle family shareholder and a member of Oerlikon's board, criticised Thomke.
Then earlier this month Oerlikon's chairman Hans Widmer said in a statement that the board did not believe the conditions were appropriate for a public listing of Bally.
Thomke then responded in a newspaper interview, saying he was disappointed with Widmer because they had agreed not to make any statements about Bally until after the August 18 meeting.
